brief: Design an interface for a "Temporal Recipe Reconstructor" that helps elderly people with dementia recreate cherished family recipes by arranging fragmented cooking memories along a spiral timeline tha

dominant_strengths: Conceptually evocative spiral metaphor with decade nodes communicates the temporal-memory framing fairly clearly
Restrained dark palette and clean sans-serif title give a calm, contemplative tone fitting reminiscence work
dominant_weaknesses: Accessibility-hostile for the stated dementia audience: tiny text, low contrast on blue chips, and dark background contradict elderly UX needs
Spatial logic is broken—decade circles overlap chaotically, ingredient cards float disconnected, and orange dot cluster on the right has no legend or affordance
Interaction model is invisible: no drag cues, no recipe canvas, no output area, so the 'reconstruction' promise is unsupported by mechanics
fix_priorities: Add a dedicated recipe-assembly canvas and explicit drag-target affordances so the core task is visible
Increase type size, contrast, and labeling for elderly users; consider a lighter, warmer palette evoking kitchen memory
Resolve the spiral overlap into a true readable arc with consistent node sizing and clear chronological order
Define and label the orange particles and brown squares or remove them—currently visual noise
rationale.norman_balance: Mildly poetic visceral surface, weak behavioral scaffolding, and decent reflective concept—but the imbalance harms the vulnerable user group it claims to serve.
rationale.intent_fit: Captures the spiral-timeline metaphor but fails the dementia-accessibility brief through low contrast, ambiguous interactions, and no visible recipe-reconstruction workflow.
